<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **45** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**56** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879`.

⛔ **20** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 60 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **187** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `38999e421cc278e623ff9d247cc201b48b2b74ff` — the merge of head `bcac5161a9cb05f64b0392be2d3e0fa02ed76dc4` into base `90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 38999e421cc278e623ff9d247cc201b48b2b74ff && git checkout 38999e421cc278e623ff9d247cc201b48b2b74ff
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879 bcac5161a9cb05f64b0392be2d3e0fa02ed76dc4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879 && git merge --no-ff bcac5161a9cb05f64b0392be2d3e0fa02ed76dc4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `72dc23a3156359a969a4603da794cc0510a8a498`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/skill.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-ai/references/_index.md + packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts, packages/spec/liveness/skill.json
Security-touching: yes

Inputs read: card #37141 (body and all five comments; no earlier contract record on it), PR #37552 (body, file list, net diff against `main`), and the 70 check-runs on this head (60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed). Contract read on `main`: ADR-0160 D1 ("Advisory reports"), D4, D8 and point 7; ADR-0150's addendum of 2026-11-25 (`ai_context` joins bucket 3), reader 2. The rest of the diff (tests, translation bundles, count pins, generated spec ledgers, changeset, `content/docs`) is the lane seat's.

`Security-touching: yes` is meant. The changed hunks of `skill.zod.ts` teach which package's pack a skill may reach (the ADR-0150 D3 closure, an isolation rule) and on which connections a record-reading prompt is offered.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `SkillSchema`: widened, right.** `context` was an unknown key of a strict object and refused; it is now accepted as a bare name (`ROUTER_ADDRESSABLE_NAME_PATTERN`, the pattern `AiContextSchema.name` uses). `refuseUnboundRecordContext` returns at once when `context` is undefined, so no skill that parsed on `main` is refused here. Nothing narrows.
- **A face is refused at `context`: right.** ADR-0150 addendum, reader 2: "The key gains no qualified spelling". A face holds `-`, the pattern does not.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/ai`: `skillBindsRecordContextTool` added, right.** It is in `api-surface/ai.json` and `export-origins/ai.json`; one predicate, read by the refusal and by lint.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/mcp`: additive, right.** `McpSkillBridge` gains two optional members; `SkillPrompt` gains optional `recordContext`; `skillPromptResult` gains an optional second parameter; `MCPServerRuntime.bridgePrompts` gains an optional fourth. A host written against `main` compiles and behaves as before.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/lint`: two rule ids added, both warnings, right.**
- **Wire: `prompts/list` gains `arguments` for a skill whose `context` resolves; `prompts/get` reads `recordId` for such a skill only.** Additive. A get with no argument builds the same result object as on `main` (`skillPromptResult`: `recordId` undefined, `text` is `instructions`).
- **Refinement not projected to JSON Schema: recorded, right.** The five new sites in `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` are the ledger of that; a JSON-Schema-only validator does not refuse the unbound skill, the server parse does.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — right. `Metadata-protocol: added` — right: one authorable key with a reader, no key removed or re-read.

The changeset bumps spec, mcp, lint, runtime and platform-objects `minor`. Spec minor matches a new authorable key and a new export. mcp and lint minor match their additions. runtime and platform-objects carry no new export (a bridge member and generated translation rows); minor is not below what they publish. `Check Changeset` is success on this head. No major is implied by the diff.

The generated mirror `skills/objectstack-ai/references/_index.md` gains one line, the transitive dependency `ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts`, which `skill.zod.ts` now imports. Its text has the form the generator prints for a file whose leading comment is not at the top (the `Exports:` form, as `field.zod.ts` and `agent.zod.ts` have on `main`). The generated-output gates on this head are success, and that is the verdict on whether it matches the build.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **SQL push-down:** no finding. The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join over record data. The one new read is the `ai_context` metadata listing, the listing `get_record_context` already selects from, read only when an offered skill names a `context`.
- **Dev open question (ledger and pin overlap with #37422 and #37366): option A is sound**, on two conditions. The second lander regenerates the spec artifacts on the merged tree and takes the printed entries, never a hand sum; and the gates run again on that head. The header total of `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` and the echo-decision count pin are single lines both PRs change, so git cannot merge them silently. `export-origins/ai.json` can merge cleanly, and the sorted union is what the build prints. A re-merge moves this head, so this record does not cover it: the new head owes a delta.
- **Deviation, pushed past the overlap check:** accepted for the reason above; the conflicts were with sibling PRs, never with `main`.
- **Deviation, surface beyond the claim:** answered by the claim amendment 7195875211. The three bridge files are the reader's wiring; without them the key has no reader at run time (ADR-0049).
- **Deviation, PR body not refreshed:** the body does not name the translation bundles, the two count pins or the final head. For the adopting seat; it does not change this verdict.
- **`Skills-docs: follow-up owed`:** flag for the adopting seat. No card number is on the line. The card's acceptance asks for the line; the owed card (`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, `references/context-packs.md`) is filed and the line rewritten to its number before ACCEPT.
- **Card's "expected" warning for `mcpPrompt: false` with `context`:** does not fire, and nothing is suppressed. `get_record_context` is in `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE` on `main` (#37190 landed first), so the name resolves for an in-product skill. The card's expectation was written before that.
- **Dev's two noted, unfiled findings** (stdio has no binding filter; lint reads the stack's own packs only): judged in ④ as S1 and S2. The general halves stay on #37609; a narrow part of each belongs to this PR.
- **Escalated:** one security-relevant reading of ADR-0160 D8 against D4 was sent to the dispatching seat out of band. It concerns the ADR's own text, not a disagreement between this code and the ADR, and is not graded here.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts`** against ADR-0160 D8 and its first consumer.

- The key, the refusal and its location hold. `SkillSchema` is the one schema behind `defineSkill`, `stack.skills` and the `/meta` save (`metadata-type-schemas.ts`), so the refusal is on every write path. The message names the tool, the key and both fixes, and is located on `tools`. In zod 4 the refinement runs after the object's own issues clear, so an author with another error sees this one second; acceptable.
- `skillBindsRecordContextTool` matches the trailing-wildcard rule `bindingEntryServed` applies (`@objectstack/mcp`), so a binding the refusal accepts is one the binding filter reads the same way.

S1 (should-fix) — the long-lived stdio door offers the record argument where `get_record_context` is not served, and three sentences of this PR say it cannot happen.
- `skill.zod.ts`, on `refuseUnboundRecordContext`: "a prompt that tells the model to call a tool the connection lacks is never offered". `liveness/skill.json` and the module doc of `skill-prompts.ts` say the same.
- `MCPServerRuntime.bridgePrompts` applies no binding filter (known, on `main`), and this PR gives its skill bridge `listContextPacks` unconditionally. So on a stdio host with no record-context service, a skill with `context` lists `recordId` and its get carries the platform-written line telling the model to call a tool the server does not register.
- The HTTP bridge does not do this: `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` assigns `listContextPacks` only inside `if (seams.recordContextTools)`, and its test has the control. The PR's own stdio parity case builds a runtime with no tools at all and gets the fixed line.
- Before this PR the stdio door relayed only the author's text. The line is the platform's, and D8 gives the binding as the thing that keeps it off such a connection; the card's acceptance has the same bullet.
- Fix, either one: offer `recordContext` on `bridgePrompts` only when that server registers `get_record_context` (this needs no general binding filter, which stays on #37609); or narrow the three sentences to the `registerSkillPrompts` surface and name the stdio gap with its card.

**`packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts`** against D8, D1's advisory and ADR-0150 addendum reader 2.

- `ai-skill-context-omitted`: the condition is D1's, sentence for sentence (a skill that binds the tool, no `context`, an object with more than one pack). It reads the stack's own packs, so a dependency's packs can only make it under-report. No false positive found. A broad wildcard (`get_*`) is advised too, which is true of the call it describes.

S2 (should-fix) — `ai-skill-context-unknown` judges ADR-0150 D3 step 1 only, and its message states a run-time consequence that is false for a dependency's pack.
- The addendum, reader 2: "The author surfaces that validate a skill judge it by the same rule." The rule's step 2 resolves a pack held in the skill's dependency closure, and `skillPromptRecordContext` does resolve it.
- For that legal configuration `os validate` reports: "so the skill's MCP prompt takes no record and its get_record_context call is refused". Neither half is true there.
- Reading the closure in lint may stay on #37609. What this PR owes is a message that does not assert the consequence when the stack cannot see the pack's holder: say that this stack does not define the pack and that the consequence holds unless a package it depends on ships it. The function's own doc already says this; the author-facing text does not.

**`packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts`, `mcp-server-runtime.ts`, `plugin.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`** against D8, sentence by sentence.

- "lists one optional prompt argument, the record id; the object is the pack's root": holds, and only when the name resolves (card item 5).
- "the skill's instructions; one fixed platform-written line; those arguments as one JSON object": holds. The line is a constant with no interpolated client value. The object is `JSON.stringify` of three members, on one line.
- "appears only there, as a JSON string value ... never joined into the line": holds. The id follows the instructions and the line, inside a quoted, escaped value; it cannot reach the instructions part. A hostile id with quotes and newlines is pinned by test and by the dev's ablation.
- "The pack itself is not placed in the prompt": holds.
- "Without the argument the prompt is what it is today": holds on both doors. The SDK passes an empty object when `arguments` is absent, so the stdio get with no arguments is served.
- Resolution: `resolvePackageScopedHolders` with the skill's package as caller. Own pack, else the one holder in the closure, else no pack. With no closure function the default is the empty set, so a package skill never resolves environment-wide. An environment skill resolves as a caller with no package. A refusal resolves to no pack. Two rows of one holder are answered as no pack before the holder source can throw.
- The pack is handed on by its face, as reader 2 says. `selectContextPack` narrows to the root first and then matches the face, so the tool reads back the pack resolved here, or refuses; I found no input that makes it read a different pack.
- "A `context` that names no pack ... no other pack is substituted": holds; no argument is offered.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/skill.form.ts`**: one plain control, with the #19331 precedent cited. The help text agrees with the schema. The form does not carry the refinement; the save refuses, located on `tools`, which the form shows on that control.

**`skills/objectstack-ai/references/_index.md`**: generated, one line, judged in ②. It teaches no security behaviour.

**`packages/spec/liveness/skill.json`**: the row names a real reader and a real validator. Its note carries the S1 sentence.

Nits, none affecting the contract:
- N1 (nit) — the prompt surface reads raw rows and does not ask `skillBindsRecordContextTool` again, so a row that reached the store unparsed with `context` and no binding would be offered the argument. It relies on the parse.
- N2 (nit) — a pack listing that throws fails `prompts/list` and every `prompts/get`, including a get with no argument and skills with no `context`, once any offered skill names one. The skill read usually fails with it.
- N3 (nit) — the two new rule ids have no `os explain` entry; `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` has one.
- N4 (nit) — `packHolderOf` and `contextPackHoldings` restate `holderOf` and `contextPackCandidates` of `@objectstack/service-record-context`. Two copies of one reading can drift.
- N5 (nit) — the record id has no length bound, and `JSON.stringify` leaves U+2028 and U+2029 unescaped. Both stay inside the string value.

No must-fix. S1 and S2 are open on this head and each earns a delta review of its fix.

Seat questions:
1. Yes at parse, which every write path goes through (`defineSkill`, `stack.skills`, the `/meta` save behind the form). The form itself does not check; the save does. The MCP doors do not re-check a raw row (N1). The error is a clear author error, located on `tools`.
2. No. A package skill reaches its own pack, then the one holder in its closure; anything else resolves to no pack, and no closure function means own package only. The prompt reads no record: the read is the tool call, as the caller. `recordId` is listed only when the pack resolves. On stdio it is listed even where the tool is not served (S1).
3. Holds on both doors. A record value cannot reach the instructions part.
4. Agrees, except the binding sentence on the stdio door (S1). The lint side departs from ADR-0150 addendum reader 2 at step 2 (S2).
5. `ai-skill-context-omitted`: right condition, no false positive. `ai-skill-context-unknown`: false positive on a dependency's pack. Neither general item needs to move off #37609; a narrow part of each is owed here (S1, S2).
6. All three right. The mirror line has the generator's form and the generated-output gates are success.
7. Sound, on the two conditions in ③; the re-merged head owes a delta.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37141-skill-context-key`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `72dc23a3156359a969a4603da794cc0510a8a498`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5

1. **Shape**: draft against `main`. 34 files, +1023/−78. GOVERNED (`skills/**` mirror, published schema), Tier H, security-touching. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added` and spec minor are right.
2. **Premise**: `SkillSchema.context`, refused at `tools` unless `get_record_context` is bound, with the pack resolved by ADR-0150 D3 through the closure, holds on every write path. The message shape holds on both doors, and a record value cannot reach the instructions.
3. **Gates**: contract record 7196143365 (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, verified on the transcript) reads PASS, with two should-fix findings owed before the handoff. CI on this head: 0 failed.
4. **Owed before the handoff** (ids from the record):
   - **S1**: the stdio door offers `recordId` and the platform line where `get_record_context` is not served. `MCPServerRuntime.bridgePrompts` has no binding filter, and its skill bridge gets `listContextPacks` unconditionally, while the HTTP bridge gates it on `seams.recordContextTools`. Offer the argument on stdio only when that server registers the tool. Pin it with the existing stdio parity test, which builds a runtime with no tools.
   - **S2**: `ai-skill-context-unknown` judges only D3 step 1, so for a pack a dependency ships, its message says the prompt "takes no record and its get_record_context call is refused", and both halves are false. Narrow the message to what lint knows (the stack's own packs). Reading the closure in lint stays on #37609.
   - **Skills-docs**: file the owed skills-docs card (`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, `references/context-packs.md`) under #37141, and rewrite the `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` line to its number.
   - **PR body**: refresh it to the final head, with the translation bundles and the two count pins.
5. **Accepted deviations and dev points**: N1 to N5 are accepted. Point 1 (`mcpPrompt: false` warning, n/a after #37190) is accepted. Point 2: the second lander of #37552, #37422 and #37366 regenerates on the merged tree and re-runs the gates, and that head owes a delta.
6. **Landing terms**: after the delta the same reviewer re-checks it. Then the seat adds `security` and hands it to the maintainer (Tier H).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5a8a19361abd5c6042f9d902d88b8d62f6782c96`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/skill.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-ai/references/_index.md + packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts, packages/spec/liveness/skill.json
Security-touching: yes

Delta review of the record on head `72dc23a3`. Read: the one commit between the two heads (8 files, +82 / -24), the net diff against `main` (34 files), the PR body as it stands, and the check-runs on this head: 62 success, 14 skipped, 2 cancelled. The two cancelled runs (`Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`) were superseded by later runs of the same names on this head, both success. Nothing in sections ①, ② and ③ of the earlier record is changed by the delta except as said below.

`Security-touching: yes` is meant, for the reason the earlier record gives: `skill.zod.ts` teaches which package's pack a skill may reach and where a record-reading prompt is offered. The delta changes a sentence of that teaching.

### ① Derived judgments

Unchanged. The delta adds no key, no export and no accept-set change. `servesTool` is private. The stdio door now offers the record argument on fewer servers than at `72dc23a3` (only where the tool is registered); against `main` that is still an addition.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — unchanged and right. `Metadata-protocol: added` — unchanged and right. The changeset keeps its five `minor` bumps; its mcp and lint paragraphs now state the stdio condition and what the unknown-context warning judges, and both agree with the code. `Check Changeset` is success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **SQL push-down:** no finding; the delta adds no read.
- **`Skills-docs:`** now reads `follow-up #37611`. The earlier flag is answered. Whether #37611 says what the line claims is the adopting seat's to read; it is outside this brief's inputs.
- **PR body:** refreshed. It names the translation bundles, both count pins, the stdio condition and the follow-up cards. The earlier flag is answered.
- **Reordering in `plugin.ts` (data tools before resources and prompts):** changes nothing else.
  - `bridgeTools` (the AI registry) still runs first, at the top of `start()`, so the rule between a bridged and a native tool of one name is met in the same order as before.
  - `bridgeDataTools` registers handlers from the bridge alone. It reads neither the runtime object view nor anything `bridgeResources` or `bridgePrompts` sets; the handlers read at call time.
  - `bridgeResources` and the `agent_prompt` registration read no tool state.
  - All of it still completes before `start()` attaches the transport, which is the one ordering the moved comment (#8034) asks for. Only the order of the boot log lines moves.
- **Whether `servesTool` sees AI-registry tools registered later:** it does not, and that is consistent. `bridgeTools` takes one snapshot of the registry, so a tool that joins the registry afterwards is never served by this server either. `servesTool` is read once, when the skill bridge is built. A host that bridged more tools after its prompts would under-offer the argument, never over-offer it; the method's doc says to bridge tools first.
- **Escalated item** of the earlier record: unchanged by the delta, still with the dispatching seat.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed.
- `bridgePrompts` gives its skill bridge `listContextPacks` only when `servesTool('get_record_context')` holds. Without the listing no skill resolves a pack, so `prompts/list` carries no argument and `skillPromptResult` ignores a sent `recordId`: the prompt is the one on `main`.
- The native tool reaches `nativeToolNames` through the names `wireBridgeTools` returns, and the new with-tool case asserts it through `tools/list`. The no-tool case pins the absence of the argument and of the line, and the dev's ablation of the gate turns it red.
- The three sentences (`skill.zod.ts`, `liveness/skill.json`, the module doc of `skill-prompts.ts`) now state the stdio condition and agree with the code. The general binding filter stays on #37609, as agreed.

S2: closed.
- The message now reads that the pack "is not in this stack's `aiContexts`: unless a dependency ships it, the MCP prompt takes no record and get_record_context is refused". The consequence is stated on its condition, and the hint names a dependency's pack as a valid target. The function doc says it judges ADR-0150 D3 step 1 only and names #37609 for the closure.
- The departure from the addendum's "judge it by the same rule" remains in the reading, and is now stated and carried by #37609. The author-facing text no longer says something false.

Nits of the earlier record: N1, N2, N3, N4 and N5 are untouched by the delta and stay nits, left as accepted deviations.
